clue.text: Crew at stern of boat evade first part of watch

indicators.note: first says the word for evade comes ahead of the crew and the stern

parts.note: to evade is to escape
a crew is the men working a vessel

indicators.note: the stern is the back end of a boat, so this takes the final letter of boat

explanation.surface: A crew huddled at the back of a boat plot to dodge the first watch of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' tempts you to read it as a period of duty on board; here it is the timepiece, and 'first' orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The escapement is the mechanism in a clock or watch that releases the gear train tick by tick.

clue.text: Unmarried Australian soprano's place of exile

indicators.note: M is the abbreviation for married, so being unmarried means dropping that letter

parts.note: Dame Nellie Melba was the famous Australian soprano

explanation.surface: A single Australian singer is said to have a favourite retreat abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping M (married) from MELBA, the stage name of the opera singer Nellie Melba, leaves the island where Napoleon was banished in 1814.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was sent to the Mediterranean island in 1814 as his first exile.

clue.text: Talk to the French going round English castle

indicators.note: going round says the talk and the French words surround the abbreviation for English

parts.note: to talk idly is to chat
au is French for 'to the'

explanation.surface: Chatting in French while touring an English fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' wraps the talk and the French around the English letter, so the E sits in the middle of the castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or grand country house.

clue.text: Have more power? Head's about to think again

indicators.note: about tells us the word for head goes around the other pieces

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
the prefix re- means again
to ponder is to think deeply

explanation.surface: A head teacher hesitates and reconsiders whether to wield more authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts REPONDER inside P-ATE. 'Head' looks like a headteacher, but it is the top of the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: To preponderate is to outweigh or dominate, to have greater force or influence.

clue.text: Government building a cleric has entered

definitions.meaning: a government department, or the offices that house it
a priest is said to have entered the church's ..., the clerical profession

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a state department and the calling of the clergy.

clue.text: Settle comfortably in finest leathers

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words finest leathers

explanation.surface: Snuggling into your best leather clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to snuggle down cosily, like a bird in its nest.

clue.text: A university in the country

parts.note: per means 'for each, a', as in 'ten pounds per person'

explanation.surface: A university somewhere in the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is not simply the letter A: it is PER, as in 'a pound a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a country in South America.

clue.text: Learned European taking wine in humble environment

indicators.note: in, with environment, says the wine sits inside the humble word
environment says the word for humble forms the surroundings

parts.note: rude in its old sense means simple and humble, as in a rude hut
it is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A continental visitor sipping wine in modest surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: The wine comes from the British bar order 'gin and it', where it means Italian vermouth; 'in' and 'environment' together signal the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned here is the adjective meaning scholarly, widely read.

clue.text: University fellow recently seen around at last

indicators.note: seen around says the word for recently encloses the fellow

parts.note: lately means recently
Tim is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A university don has lately been spotted around the campus at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' suggests a college fellow, but it is just a man's name; 'seen around' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimately means finally, in the end.

clue.text: Effrontery of woman about to destroy notes

indicators.note: about says the woman's name goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Bess is a woman's name, short for Elizabeth
to raze is to destroy completely
n. is the abbreviation for note, so two notes give NN

explanation.surface: The cheek of a woman who sets about shredding banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' look like music or money; here each is just the abbreviation n. 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Effrontery is shameless boldness, the quality of being bold-faced and cheeky.

clue.text: Give up completely, lacking energy

indicators.note: lacking says the letter for energy is removed from the word

parts.note: quite means completely, as in quite right
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Stop altogether once you run out of steam.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to abandon or stop doing something.

clue.text: Get like Williams — stop working properly

parts.note: go can mean get or become, as in go bald
a Williams is a variety of pear, so something like it is shaped like a pear

explanation.surface: Taking after someone called Williams, then failing to function.
explanation.walkthrough: Williams looks like a person; it is the Williams pear, a common variety (called Bartlett in the US). Becoming pear-shaped is the British idiom for things going wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means to go wrong or fall apart.

clue.text: Principal character, a priestess of Aphrodite

definitions.meaning: in Greek legend Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit her, a priestess of Aphrodite at Sestos

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a story's lead role and the legendary lover of Leander.

clue.text: Most of drift in retired woman's subtle reasoning

indicators.note: in says the trimmed word sits inside the reversed name
retired means drawn back, so the woman's name is written backwards

parts.note: Molly is a woman's name, with the possessive s

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the drift of an argument is its gist

explanation.surface: A retired woman's clever argument mostly drifts off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the woman's name into SYLLOM; 'Most of' trims drift's synonym to three letters; 'in' places them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllogism is a piece of formal deductive reasoning from two premises, also used of specious argument.

clue.text: Source of painting old archdeacon found in spring

indicators.note: found in says the old and archdeacon pieces sit inside the spring word

parts.note: to prance is to spring about
Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: An old clergyman's painting turned up in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: VEN is short for 'the Venerable', the title of a Church of England archdeacon. 'Spring' looks like the season; it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Provenance is the recorded history of where a work of art came from.

clue.text: Without hesitation, catches game

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the catches enclose the hesitation

parts.note: a catch is a musical round, a song sung in overlapping parts
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone takes catches unhesitatingly in a ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hesitation' reads as 'promptly', but 'Without' means outside. ROUNDERS is a British bat-and-ball game like baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounders is a bat-and-ball game, an example of a sport.

clue.text: Further airing of broadcast about fuel

parts.note: re means about, as in business letters
peat is dug and burned as fuel

explanation.surface: A programme about fuel gets shown again.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun of a programme is a second showing on air.

clue.text: Like good conductor, satisfied everyone initially in choir

parts.note: to satisfy a demand is to meet it, past tense met
all means everyone

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of the words in and choir

explanation.surface: A good conductor pleased everyone at the start in the choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' suggests a choir leader; it is a material carrying electricity or heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Metals conduct electricity and heat well, so something with metal-like qualities is a good conductor.

clue.text: Sort of light a good person put in part of church

indicators.note: put in says the good person goes inside the light

parts.note: a Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol
St, short for saint, stands for a good person

explanation.surface: A flare and a saintly figure are set inside a church room.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a signal flare, named after its inventor Edward Very.
explanation.definitionFit: The vestry is a room in a church where vestments are kept and clergy robe.

clue.text: Material in H. H. Munro originally considered no good

indicators.note: in says the first letter goes inside the writer's pen name

parts.note: H. H. Munro wrote short stories under the pen name Saki

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of considered

explanation.surface: A story by Saki thought to be worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: SAKI is the pen name of the Edwardian short-story writer H. H. Munro; 'in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacking is coarse cloth such as hessian used for sacks.

clue.text: Rare slip potentially produces act of retaliation

indicators.note: potentially says the letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual mistake might provoke revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is a retaliatory act of revenge.

clue.text: Batsman facing bowler, or one who's out?

definitions.meaning: in cricket the batter currently receiving the ball
a worker who has walked out on strike

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batter receiving the ball is the striker; 'out' looks like a dismissal but means on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the receiving batter and a worker taking industrial action.

clue.text: Rush madly into long-term occupation

definitions.meaning: to hurtle along wildly out of control

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for hurtling headlong and a noun for one's working life.

clue.text: Organised action involving Scotsman in plant

indicators.note: involving says the shuffled letters enclose the Scotsman
organised says the letters of action are arranged anew

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Coordinated activity by a Scot inside a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' turns the fodder into NICOTA; 'involving' puts the Scot inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotiana is the tobacco genus, including ornamental flowering tobacco.

clue.text: Hogarth's first painting, possibly — a male deer

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Hogarth's

parts.note: painting is one example of art, hence possibly

explanation.surface: Hogarth's earliest picture may show a stag.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is hidden inside 'Hogarth' itself, a tempting but wrong route; the parse is H plus ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A hart is an adult male red deer, a stag.

clue.text: Source of dye popular over in Alabama

indicators.note: in says the reversed word sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

indicators.note: over says the word for popular is turned back to front

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A dye source is popular across Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the popular word into NI, and 'in' puts it inside the state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant, from which a blue dye is made.

clue.text: Bring down fastening device

definitions.meaning: to catch or bring someone down
a metal pin hammered in to join wood

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to catch out or floor someone and the pin used to fix timber.

clue.text: Agreement accepted by two writers with cultivated accents

parts.note: H. G. Wells is a writer

indicators.note: accepted by says the agreement is taken inside the second writer

parts.note: a pen is a writer, the instrument that writes
OK signals agreement

explanation.surface: A pact signed by two authors with polished voices.
explanation.walkthrough: One writer is an author, the other a writing instrument; 'accepted by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-spoken means speaking in a refined, educated manner.

clue.text: Ridge on which one is ill at ease?

definitions.text: Ridge on which one is ill at ease?

parts.words: Ridge on which one is ill at ease?
parts.note: a ridge or border, and the idiom for being nervous is to be 'on' this kind of narrow ridge

explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a sharp ridge or rim, and to be on one is to be nervous.

clue.text: Wild leopard tangles with cur, following established method

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters are thrown into disorder
tangles with suggests the two words become knotted together and rearranged

explanation.surface: An untamed big cat fights a mongrel dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' and 'tangles with' both mark an anagram of LEOPARD plus CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Procedural means relating to set procedure, done by the book.
